title: Father of All, Whose Cares Extend
description: Father of All, Whose Cares Extend in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Alexander Pope wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 483 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of all, whose cares ex-tend To earth's re-mo-test shore, Through ev-ery age let praise as-cend, And ev-ery clime a-dore.

lines: Father of all, whose cares extend
To earth's remotest shore,
Through every age let praise ascend,
And every clime adore.
Mean though I am, not wholly so,
Since quickened by thy breath;
Lord, lead me wheresoe'er I go,
Through this day's life or death.
Teach me to feel another's woe,
To hide the fault I see;
That mercy I to others show,
That mercy show to me.
If I am right, thy grace impart
Still in the right to stay;
If I am wrong, O teach my heart
To find that better way.
What conscience dictates to be done,
Or warns me not to do,
This teach me more than hell to shun,
That more than heaven pursue.

licence: Public domain: Alexander Pope died in 1744.
credits: Words by Alexander Pope (1688–1744), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
